decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'Flow 1 — saving a link... paste any web link... click Save link... link appear immediately at the top'. Round 4 client: 'the link appearing immediately feels right'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url conforms to REF-BM-01; recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presented showing a 'name/title for each link (guessed from the address)'. Round 4 client: 'I'd want the app to pick up the page's actual title rather than guessing it from the address, with a way for me to change it if needed.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Guessing title from the address diverges from REF-BM-02 (auto-collect the target page's real title). Client rejects the guess and supplies the reference-conforming behaviour (fetch the actual page title, plus editability), so corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'I put the newest saved link at the top... Is newest-first the order you'd expect?' Round 4 client: 'newest-first is what I'd expect.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Newest-first (date-added descending) is a conforming default ordering under REF-BM-22; the default itself does not contradict the reference. A user-selectable sort key was never presented (coverage gap), but the presented default conforms — not_divergent.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker: real title fetched then 'click Rename... change the name... press Save name'. Round 5 client: 'Being able to correct the title afterward is what matters most.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (revised presentation resolving the round-4 correction). Editing the auto-collected title before/after save conforms to REF-BM-03/04; bare approval of a conforming presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker: 'click + add tag, type a word... It becomes a rounded tag chip. Add a second one.' Round 6 client: 'Free-form tags... feel right, and adding them on the saved link is fine.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09. (Lower-casing and per-card placement are orthogonal/equivalent implementation choices, excluded.)

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presented 'free-form tags you type yourself' with no suggestions, asking whether typing your own tags is right. Round 6 client: 'As I type, though, I'd like to see matching tags I've already used so I can reuse them consistently instead of accidentally creating near-duplicates.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Free-form tag entry with no autocomplete diverges from REF-BM-10 (offer existing tags as autocomplete on entry). Client supplies the missing reference-conforming behaviour (as-you-type existing-tag suggestions), so corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: 'start typing a... a small list should drop down showing your existing matching tag (article). Click it to reuse it exactly.' Round 7 client: 'Yes, that matches what I wanted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (revised presentation resolving the round-6 correction). Autocomplete now conforms to REF-BM-10; bare approval of the conforming fix, counted once here without re-counting the earlier corrective.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker: 'type part of a title or address into the Search box. The list narrows... Search finds tags too.' Round 8 client: 'this feels straightforward and sufficient for finding a saved link.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. One-box full-text matching over title/address conforms (partially) to REF-BM-12; the presented basic search itself is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker stated the full scope: 'Search looks across title, web address, and tags together (one box, not separate fields), matching as you type.' Round 8 client: 'Yes, this feels straightforward and sufficient for finding a saved link.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented search scope implicitly excludes the reference's #tag syntax (REF-BM-14), AND/OR/NOT/parenthesised operators (REF-BM-15), and quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16). The client approved as 'sufficient' without expressing any of these expectations, so the divergence passes unexpressed (approval does not establish awareness).

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker: 'click a tag chip on any link. The list narrows to just links with that tag.' Round 8 client: 'I like having one search box, clickable tag filters, a visible count...'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Click-a-tag filtering to only that tag's bookmarks conforms to REF-BM-11.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: 'Every saved link is To read by default when you save it.' Round 9 client: 'I wouldn't want every saved link to start as To read... I'd like to choose whether a link goes into the read-later list when I save it, and still be able to change that afterward.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Defaulting every bookmark to unread/read-later diverges from REF-BM-17, where read-later is a chosen state, not a universal default. Client rejects the default and supplies opt-in-at-save with later toggling, so corrective/correct.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker: 'three view tabs: All, To read, and Read... unread count badge... marking read is fully reversible.' Round 9 client: 'The views, count, and reversible read status feel right.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Separate unread view (REF-BM-18) and reversible mark-as-read (REF-BM-19) conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 10 maker: 'the read-later checkbox is unchecked by default, so a link only enters your reading pile when you deliberately opt in.' Round 10 client: 'Yes, that matches what I want.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (revised presentation resolving the round-9 correction). Opt-in read-later now conforms to REF-BM-17; bare approval of the conforming fix, not re-counted as an opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker offered a choice for Edge 4: 'that the app quietly lets you have two copies, or that it notices the duplicate and warns you.' Round 11 client: 'For a duplicate, don't create another copy. Let me know it already exists and take me to the existing bookmark so I can edit it instead.'
decisions.note: Specification gate (edge-case decision). One offered alternative (allow two copies) diverges from REF-BM-06; the other conforms. The client selects the reference-conforming alternative and specifies guiding to edit the existing bookmark — corrective/select; the offered decision is marked diverged=true per the select rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: 'you'll see... This link is already saved... the page scrolls to the existing bookmark... its title opens ready for you to edit.' Round 12 client: 'Taking me directly to the existing bookmark and opening it for editing is clear and avoids clutter.'
decisions.note: Prototype review (revised presentation resolving the round-11 selection). Duplicate url converges to editing the existing bookmark, conforming to REF-BM-06; not re-counted as a separate opportunity.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker: 'click the new Delete button... it asks Delete this bookmark?... deleted bookmarks should disappear everywhere, including the To read count.' Round 13 client: 'I want confirmation before permanent deletion, and deleted bookmarks should disappear everywhere.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delete conforms to REF-BM-05; the confirm step and cascade-to-count are orthogonal/equivalent enhancements, not divergences.
